issues.title: Right-hand-side time projector has the wrong spatial target

failure_location.quote:
Let~$\Pizpbftmo$ denote the piecewise~$L^2$ projector onto~$\Pbb_{\pnt-1}(\In; \HozOmega)$
for all $n=1,\dots,N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The old source permits f in L2(0,T;L2(Omega)), and even the stronger a posteriori assumption gives only H1 regularity in time with values in L2(Omega). For an admissible time-independent f(t)=g with g in L2(Omega) but not H_0^1(Omega), the asserted projector onto time polynomials with H_0^1 coefficients is not defined. Consequently rhs:semidiscrete and the discrete-star identity cannot be used as printed. Projecting only in time with spatial target L2(Omega) gives the required orthogonality against the test functions.
issues.overall_effect: The projected right-hand side and the ensuing a posteriori reliability proof were not well-defined for the paper's allowed source data. The semidiscrete variational method itself remains meaningful.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In rhs:semidiscrete, define the temporal L2 projector with target P_{p_n^t-1}(I_n;L2(Omega)), rather than P_{p_n^t-1}(I_n;H_0^1(Omega)), and use that reading in the discrete-star identity and both reliability propositions.
issues.why_classification: The old data assumption, the L2 right-hand-side pairing, and the same projector's L2-valued use elsewhere uniquely force this spatial target. The H_0^1 target is an ill-typed codomain transcription; correcting it restores the stated orthogonality without changing any inference or guarantee.

issues.title: Cumulative jump term missing from the stability proof
issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts control of the sum of all derivative jumps from 1 through m. At n=m, inequality-step-n controls only the jump at t_{m-1}, while the preceding node-energy estimate as printed contains no jumps from the first m-1 slabs. Consequently, the displayed combination cannot yield the asserted accumulated sum. The standard energy identity obtained by testing with the time derivative does supply those earlier jumps, which is the term added in the revision.
issues.overall_effect: The cumulative-jump part of the stability theorem, and the corresponding jump-sum conclusion in lemma:estimates-xih, was unproved. The energy-norm part used by the later abstract and hp-convergence theorems remains obtainable after dropping the unsupported positive sum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Derive the standard node-energy estimate by testing with the time derivative and summing through slab n-1 while retaining the term (1/4) times the sum of the derivative-jump norms over ell=1,...,n-1. Combining it with inequality-step-n at n=m then supplies the complete sum through m; carry the same restored estimate into lemma:estimates-xih.
issues.why_classification: The missing cumulative term must be checked and restored mathematically, so this is not merely a transcriptional typo. The required calculation is a short, routine local energy identity that restores the stability theorem and dependent lemma at their original strength without a new lemma, changed rate, or altered method.

issues.title: The admitted first-slab degree-one case is unsupported

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The space of polynomials of nonnegative degree~$\p$ over~$D$ is~$\Pbb_\p(D)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Because the old lower bound starts at n=2, p_1^t=1 is admissible. On I_1, the integrated-projector definitions then invoke P_{-1} and P_{-2}, although the source defines polynomial spaces only for nonnegative degree and omits the moment only for p_n^t=2. The reconstruction branch is independently defective in the same regime: c2 has no p=1 case, and for X=R, I_1=(0,1), V(t)=at, and incoming derivative d not equal to a, the p=1 reconstruction conditions give V-hat(1)=(a+d)/2 rather than V(1)=a, contradicting its endpoint property. Thus the old formal chain does not cover an admitted input.
issues.overall_effect: The old statements leave their projector, reconstruction, a priori, and reliability chains undefined or unproved when only the first slab has degree one. Results in the all-degrees-at-least-two regime are unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen the global degree condition to p_n^t>=2 for every n=1,...,N, so that the first slab and all later slabs satisfy the degree assumptions inherited by the integrated projector, reconstruction, approximation, convergence, and reliability results.
issues.why_classification: The repair is local and leaves a recognizably identical chain for degrees at least two, so no global reconstruction is needed. It nevertheless removes the coherent and natural first-slab degree-one regime from every listed result; that meaningful but limited scope loss prevents treatment as a typo or minor technical qualification.

issues.title: Integrated Thomée identities are undefined on a general Banach space

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Given a Banach space~$\mathcal X$,
we introduce an operator~$\Pcalpbftt$

issues.failure_explanation: The old subsection assumes only a real Banach space with a norm, but defines orthogonality through an L2 inner product and states the formal lemma using both an L2(I_n;X) inner product and an inner product on X. Such operations are not defined for a generic Banach space, so the operator used by the lemma is not well-defined under its inherited hypothesis. Restricting X to a Hilbert space with the indicated inner product makes the construction and proof meaningful.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract integrated-Thomée identities and approximation results were not established at their advertised Banach-space generality. Their concrete uses in the paper employ Hilbert spaces and survive the restriction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume throughout the integrated-Thomee subsection that X is a real Hilbert space with a specified inner product inducing its norm, and let that hypothesis be inherited by the defining identity, lemma:Schoetzau-Schwab, lemma:Schoetzau-Schwab-derivatives, and proposition:Pcaltildept-L2-approx.
issues.why_classification: This contained assumption change makes all inner products and proofs valid and preserves the identities and approximation rates on the Hilbert-space domain. However, replacing the explicitly advertised Banach-space domain by Hilbert spaces excludes a broad natural class, so it is a limited substantive weakening rather than a typo or lossless minor repair.

issues.title: Initial-displacement H1 rate is overstated by one spatial order
issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds the H1-seminorm error of a degree-p_x elliptic projection by h raised to min(p_x+1,s-1/2). For example, on a uniform mesh of (0,1), with p_x=1 and u_0=x(1-x), every continuous piecewise-linear approximation has H1 error of order h, whereas the old estimate with s=5/2 predicts order h squared. Thus estimate-gimel1 is a false approximation step; the attainable exponent is min(p_x,s-1/2).
issues.overall_effect: One initial-displacement contribution in the hp theorem is assigned an unattainable extra spatial order. The remaining terms and the fixed-degree corollary retain their stated overall order after correction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the hp theorem, specialize the initial term before applying the loose bound from the abstract estimate: since u_{0,h}=Pi_h^E u_0 and the integrated time projector interpolates the left endpoint, xi_h(0)=0 exactly. Replace estimate-gimel1 by this cancellation and omit that contribution from the proof; the theorem's displayed right-hand side may remain unchanged as it only adds a nonnegative term, and the corollary requires no change.
issues.why_classification: The printed spatial approximation inference is genuinely false and therefore is not a typo. Nevertheless, the old source supplies a short local bypass through the exact initial-projector cancellation, which proves the same hp theorem and preserves all stated rates without weakening the erroneous exponent or introducing new analysis.

issues.failure_explanation: For an arbitrary Banach space X, the quantities denoted by inner products in definition-Rcalppo are undefined. The proposition's proof also chooses a reconstruction error as a test vector and infers equality from its squared norm, which requires an inner product inducing the norm. Hence the reconstruction used by the proposition is not defined under the old hypothesis. The revised Hilbert assumption validates those operations.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract smoothness proposition and reconstruction-norm lemma were not established for non-Hilbert Banach spaces. Their later L2-based wave-equation applications remain covered after the restriction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume in definition-Rcalppo and its inherited results that X is a real Hilbert space with a specified inner product inducing the norm. Under that hypothesis, retain proposition:smoothness-reconstruction and lemma:properties-a-la-Wihler with their existing conclusions and constants.
issues.why_classification: The Hilbert hypothesis is a contained repair that validates the reconstruction, endpoint argument, and norm identities without changing their conclusions or rates. It nonetheless withdraws the expressly claimed and substantial non-Hilbert Banach-space domain, leaving a comparable but genuinely narrower abstract chain; this is limited scope loss and hence moderate.

issues.title: Rate remark assigns the c4 loss to T6 instead of T5
issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that the p_n=2 scaling of c4 lowers the convergence rate of T6. The old derivation actually introduces c4 only when bounding T5; bound-T6 contains tau_m cubed times c2 and no c4 factor. The material difference is that the exceptional one-order degradation and the subsequent rate comparison concern T5, not T6.
issues.overall_effect: The remark misidentifies which local estimator contribution suffers the p_n=2 rate loss, but the estimator formulas and reliability propositions themselves are unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every reference to T6 in the affected rate remark by T5, including the statements about the p_n^t=2 loss, the higher-degree rate, and the comparison with the error rate.
issues.why_classification: The old displayed bounds uniquely identify T5 as the only term containing c4, while bound-T6 contains no c4 factor. The repeated T6 label is therefore a transcriptional misidentification that an intended reader can correct directly; no estimator formula, proof, or guarantee changes.
